flow_transcript_slices.question: Tell me about a time a child was having a really hard moment emotionally. What did you notice about what they were feeling, and how did you respond?
flow_transcript_slices.candidate_transcript:
[Q3 Attempt 1]
Recently, I had a child. Mom kind of told us that they were having problems like her and dad, so I noticed that his behavior was changing a lot, and he was becoming more aggressive with the children. I mean, I would sit him down, but I wouldn't just sit him down by himself. I would actually sit down with him and talk to him and tell him, everything's okay. Relax your body. Calm yourself. It's fine. Don't worry. Don't get upset because I knew there was more going on than just...

flow_transcript_slices.question: Tell me about a time you felt overwhelmed at work with children present. What did you do to manage yourself?
flow_transcript_slices.candidate_transcript:
[Q4 Attempt 1]
So right now I'm dealing with the problem where I feel like there's not enough of us and we're taking in all these children. And a lot of them, they have autism, either like full blown autism or they're on the spectrum. And it's frustrating for me to have to try to get through a day and then I can't because they they can't keep up. We're not qualified to have special needs children with us. So they can't keep up and it becomes a huge distraction. Usually what I do is just move on from activity and just go to something more play based.

flow_transcript_slices.question: Imagine you’re caring for a child who clearly does not want to be touched during a routine task, like diapering, helping with clothing, or guiding them physically. They are pulling away or saying no. Walk me through exactly what you would do, step by step
flow_transcript_slices.candidate_transcript:
[Q5 Attempt 1]
Well, I'll start by trying to assure them that everything's okay. I usually would just give them space for a little bit and then just let them ease on their own. If that doesn't work, a lot of the times if there's another adult present, I'll have them help me. But if there isn't, I honestly just wait, give them space, let them breathe, let them relax. And I'll just try to keep reassuring.

flow_transcript_slices.question: Tell me about a time something didn’t go as planned at work and your role in it. How did you handle the responsibility piece?

flow_transcript_slices.question: Tell me about a time you had to work closely with another adult in a challenging situation. How did you navigate it?
